Make the discretization step and the input/output projections functions of the current token: $$\Delta_t = \mathrm{softplus}\big(s_\Delta(x_t)\big) \in \mathbb{R}^{d}_{>0}, \qquad B_t = W_B x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{N}, \qquad C_t = W_C x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{N},$$ with $A \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times N}$ (diagonal, one $N$-state system per channel) left input-independent. Discretize per step: $\bar A_t = \exp(\Delta_t \odot A)$ and, using the first-order simplification $A^{-1}(e^{\Delta A}-1)\approx\Delta$ valid for small $\Delta A$, $\bar B_t = \Delta_t B_t$. The recurrence $h_t = \bar A_t \odot h_{t-1} + \bar B_t x_t$ carries a state $h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times N}$, read out as $y_t = h_t C_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d}$, and is now time-varying.

Read $\Delta_t$ as a soft gate. Large $\Delta_t$ makes $\bar A_t = e^{\Delta_t A} \to 0$ and $\bar B_t$ large: reset the state and write this token in. Small $\Delta_t$ makes $\bar A_t \to 1$ and $\bar B_t \to 0$: hold the state, ignore this token. That is an LSTM's forget/input gate rediscovered through the discretization: selectivity and gating are one story.

Three things break. First, there is no longer a single kernel $K$, so the FFT convolution is gone — every position has a different filter. Second, the computation is genuinely a $T$-step recurrence. Third, the discretized tensors $\bar A_t, \bar B_t$ have shape $(B, T, d, N)$: at $B=64$, $T=4096$, $d=2048$, $N=16$ in fp32 that is $64\cdot 4096\cdot 2048\cdot 16 \cdot 4 = 3.4\times 10^{10}$ bytes, roughly 34 GB. Materializing it is not an option. Certain

Mamba's answer is a fused kernel in the FlashAttention style of Chapter 31: load $A$, $\Delta$, $B$, $C$ from HBM into SRAM, perform discretization, scan and output contraction there, write only $y$ back, and recompute the intermediates during the backward pass instead of storing them. The arithmetic is unchanged; the memory traffic drops by a factor of roughly $N$.

21.5.1 The Parallel Scan

The scan itself is the mathematically interesting part. Each step is an affine map $f_t(h) = a_t h + b_t$, and affine maps are closed under composition:

$$(f_t \circ f_s)(h) = a_t(a_s h + b_s) + b_t = (a_t a_s)h + (a_t b_s + b_t).$$

So define $\oplus$ on parameter pairs by $(a_s,b_s)\oplus(a_t,b_t) = (a_t a_s,\; a_t b_s + b_t)$, with identity $(1,0)$. Function composition is associative, hence so is $\oplus$, and $h_t$ is the $t$-th prefix of a scan under $\oplus$. This is exactly the property $\tanh$ destroys, and exactly the reason removing the nonlinearity between steps was worth the expressivity.

Blelloch's work-efficient scan realizes it in two passes over a balanced binary tree. The up-sweep computes, at each internal node, the $\oplus$-aggregate of its subtree, in $\lceil\log_2 T\rceil$ levels. The root is then set to the identity and the down-sweep pushes prefixes back down: a node with incoming prefix $p$ gives $p$ to its left child and $p \oplus (\text{left aggregate})$ to its right, again in $\lceil\log_2 T\rceil$ levels. Total work is $2T-2$ applications of $\oplus$ — linear, unlike the $O(T\log T)$ of the naive Hillis–Steele scan — at depth $2\lceil\log_2 T\rceil$. At $T=4096$ that is 12 levels each way instead of 4096 sequential steps.

Common Pitfall

Never form $\prod_{r=s+1}^{t}a_r$ by multiplying, and never exponentiate before masking. Work in log space with $g_t = \sum_{r\le t}\log a_r$, so the product is $\exp(g_t - g_s)$. Two failures follow from getting this wrong. A direct cumprod of a few thousand factors below one underflows to exactly $0.0$ in fp32 within a few hundred steps, silently truncating memory and zeroing the gradient. And in the SSD form below, computing exp(g[:,None]-g[None,:]) and then applying the causal mask overflows to inf in the upper triangle — where the exponent is large and positive — and inf multiplied by a zero mask is NaN, not zero. Mask the exponent first, exponentiate second.

21.6 Mamba-2 and Structured State-Space Duality

Mamba-2 restricts the state transition further: instead of a diagonal $A_t$, use a scalar times the identity, $\bar A_t = a_t I_N$. It is a real loss; the payoff is that the model becomes a matrix multiplication.

Theorem 21.2 (Structured state-space duality)

Let $h_t = a_t h_{t-1} + B_t x_t^{\top} \in \mathbb{R}^{N\times P}$ with $h_{-1}=0$, $a_t\in\mathbb{R}$, $B_t, C_t \in \mathbb{R}^{N}$, $x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{P}$, and $y_t = C_t^{\top}h_t$. Stack $B,C \in \mathbb{R}^{T\times N}$, $X,Y \in \mathbb{R}^{T\times P}$ and define $L\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times T}$ by $L_{ts} = \prod_{r=s+1}^{t}a_r$ for $s\le t$ and $0$ otherwise. Then $$Y = \big(L \odot CB^{\top}\big)\,X .$$ Moreover $L$ is 1-semiseparable: every submatrix lying strictly below the diagonal has rank exactly one.

Proof. Unrolling gives $h_t = \sum_{s\le t}\big(\prod_{r=s+1}^{t}a_r\big)B_s x_s^{\top}$, so $y_t = C_t^\top h_t = \sum_{s\le t} L_{ts}\,(C_t^{\top}B_s)\,x_s$, which is row $t$ of $(L\odot CB^\top)X$. For semiseparability, write $g_t = \sum_{r\le t}\log a_r$; then for $s \le t$, $L_{ts} = e^{g_t}e^{-g_s}$, an outer product of $(e^{g_t})_t$ with $(e^{-g_s})_s$ restricted to any strictly-lower block. $\blacksquare$

Compare to causal attention, which before row normalization is $Y = \big(M \odot \exp(QK^\top/\sqrt{d_k})\big)V$ with $M$ the binary causal mask — masking must precede the softmax, not follow it, or the rows renormalize over positions the model cannot see. Same shape, same masked-quadratic-form skeleton. The differences are exactly two: $M$ is replaced by a decayed mask $L$, and the exponential and its row normalizer are deleted. Deleting the softmax is what makes the recurrence associative and therefore scannable; keeping a mask that is 1-semiseparable rather than binary is what gives the recurrence a finite state. Attention with a $T$-growing KV cache and an SSM with an $N\times P$ state are the two evaluation orders of the same matrix.

Three payoffs. Speed: the practical algorithm is neither form but a chunked hybrid — split the sequence into blocks of length $Q$, compute the diagonal blocks with the quadratic form (dense matmuls, which run on tensor cores at full rate) and the off-diagonal blocks through the rank-one structure, carrying one state across chunk boundaries. Mamba-2's layer is reported 2–8$\times$ faster than Mamba-1's scan at equal quality. Verify Capacity: because the expensive part is now matmul rather than a memory-bound scan, $N$ can grow from 16 to 256 at modest cost, which recovers most of what the scalar-identity restriction gave up. Systems reuse: multi-head, grouped-query sharing of $B$ and $C$, tensor parallelism and sequence parallelism all transfer unchanged from the attention stack.

21.7 Linear Attention, RWKV, RetNet, and the Unified View

Theorem 21.2 makes an entire literature collapse into one axis: what structure does the state-transition matrix have? Every model below is $S_t = G_t\,S_{t-1} + (\text{rank-1 write})$ read out by a query, differing only in $G_t$.

ModelTransition $G_t$Input-dependent?Consequence
Linear attention (2020)$I$nono forgetting; state saturates
RetNet$\gamma I$, $\gamma$ fixed per headnofixed exponential decay; still LTI
RWKV-4$e^{-w}I$, learned per channelnochannelwise decay, LTI
S4 / S4D$e^{\Delta A}$ diagonal, fixednoFFT convolution available
Mamba$\exp(\Delta_t \odot A)$ diagonalyesselective; scan only
Mamba-2 / SSD$a_t I$yesmasked matmul; large $N$
DeltaNet$I - \beta_t k_tk_t^{\top}$yesrank-1 update; state tracking
Softmax attention— (state grows with $t$)—exact recall, $O(T)$ cache

The table is a tradeoff. Richer $G_t$ means more expressive state dynamics and a more expensive scan; DeltaNet's non-diagonal $G_t$ buys genuine state tracking at the price of a much harder parallel form — but only with $\beta_t$ extended to $2$, making $I-\beta_tk_tk_t^\top$ a reflection: Grazzi et al. (2024) show $\beta_t\in[0,1]$ still fails parity, while eigenvalues reaching $-1$ compose permutations, which diagonal transitions provably cannot. Likely

21.8 Hybrids and the Recall–Efficiency Tradeoff

The central claim is contested. Contested

For. At small-to-mid scale, selective SSMs match or beat transformers on next-token perplexity trained on the same data, and the inference economics are not close: decoding is $O(1)$ memory per token against a KV cache linear in context, giving several-fold throughput at long context. NVIDIA's Nemotron-H family replaces most self-attention layers with Mamba-2 blocks and reports up to $3\times$ faster inference at matched or better accuracy against Qwen-2.5 and Llama-3.1 baselines. Verify

Against. The state is $N\times P$ scalars, a number fixed at design time and independent of $T$. Jelassi et al. (2024) prove a two-layer transformer can copy strings of exponential length while any fixed-state recurrent model is information-theoretically bounded by its state size, and confirm the gap empirically on pretrained models: transformers dominate at copying and at retrieving arbitrary spans from context. Perplexity averages over a distribution in which exact recall is rare; the tasks people actually deploy — long-document question answering, in-context learning from many examples, agentic tool traces — are recall-heavy.

The decisive evidence is the deployment record. Essentially every serious production model in this family is a hybrid: Jamba interleaves attention with Mamba at roughly 1:7, Nemotron-H keeps about 8% attention, Falcon-H1 fuses the two in parallel within a layer, Zamba shares a global attention block. A hybrid is strictly more complex and more expensive than a pure SSM. That anyone builds one is the strongest available argument that the pure claim is false. My position: selective SSMs do not match transformers as a drop-in replacement, but a mostly-SSM hybrid beats both pure architectures on the quality-per-throughput frontier, and that is the real result. A handful of full-attention layers supplies the exact recall; the SSM layers supply cheap long-range mixing. What would change my mind: a pure SSM at $\ge$7B matching a same-data transformer on long-context needle retrieval and multi-hop recall, not perplexity.

The line has not stopped. Mamba-3 (Lahoti, Li, Chen, Wang, Bick, Kolter, Dao, Gu; arXiv 2603.15569, ICLR 2026; CMU, Princeton, Together AI, Cartesia) is motivated explicitly by inference cost rather than pretraining loss, and makes three changes to Mamba-2. It replaces the first-order Euler-style step of Definition 21.2 with an exponential-trapezoidal discretization, raising the local truncation error from $O(\Delta^2)$ to $O(\Delta^3)$ and implicitly convolving adjacent inputs into the state write — which lets it drop the short causal conv1d entirely. It generalizes the scalar-identity transition $a_t I$ to a complex-valued one — a rotation-scaling, shown equivalent to a real SSM with data-dependent RoPE applied to $B$ and $C$ — which restores state tracking: Mamba-3 solves parity and modular arithmetic, where Mamba-2 and other real-valued linear models are at chance. And it adds a MIMO structure that raises arithmetic intensity during decode. Reported: comparable perplexity to Mamba-2 at half the state size, +0.6 points average downstream over Gated DeltaNet at 1.5B with the MIMO variant reaching +1.8, and lower per-token decode latency. Verify Do not treat Mamba-2 as the frontier.

Artifact 21.1 — Three Equivalences: Scan, Convolution, and the SSD Duality

Pure NumPy, float64. A selective SSM computed twice (sequential recurrence, Blelloch scan); an S4D kernel applied three ways (FFT, naive Toeplitz, complex recurrence); Theorem 21.2 checked against the masked matmul, plus an SVD test of 1-semiseparability.

import time
import numpy as np

try:
    import torch
except ImportError:
    torch = None

RNG = np.random.default_rng(0)

# --- (A) Selective scan: h_t = abar_t (*) h_{t-1} + bbar_t ------------------
def make_selective(T, P, N, rng):
    A = -np.exp(rng.normal(0.0, 0.5, size=(P, N)))          # A < 0: stable poles
    x = rng.normal(size=(T, P))
    # Delta = softplus(.) > 0 is the selectivity: per-token, per-channel step.
    Delta = np.log1p(np.exp(rng.normal(-0.5, 0.5, size=(T, P))))
    B = rng.normal(size=(T, N)) / np.sqrt(N)
    C = rng.normal(size=(T, N)) / np.sqrt(N)
    D = rng.normal(size=(P,))
    abar = np.exp(Delta[:, :, None] * A[None, :, :])        # (T,P,N)
    bbar = Delta[:, :, None] * B[:, None, :] * x[:, :, None]
    return abar, bbar, C, D, x

def scan_sequential(abar, bbar, C, D, x):
    """The obvious O(T) loop. Depth T: step t waits on step t-1."""
    T, P, N = abar.shape
    h = np.zeros((P, N)); y = np.empty((T, P))
    for t in range(T):
        h = abar[t] * h + bbar[t]
        y[t] = h @ C[t]
    return y + D * x

def blelloch_scan(a, b):
    """Work-efficient inclusive scan of the affine maps f_t(h) = a_t*h + b_t.
    (a_L,b_L) o (a_R,b_R) = (a_R a_L, a_R b_L + b_R), identity (1, 0).
    2T-2 total applications, ceil(log2 T) levels each way."""
    n = a.shape[0]
    m = 1 << (n - 1).bit_length()                # pad to a power of two
    tail = (m - n,) + a.shape[1:]
    A  = np.concatenate([a, np.ones(tail, a.dtype)])
    Bv = np.concatenate([b, np.zeros(tail, b.dtype)])
    a0, b0 = A.copy(), Bv.copy()
    s = 2                                        # ---- up-sweep ----
    while s <= m:
        h = s >> 1
        aL, bL = A[h - 1::s], Bv[h - 1::s]
        aR, bR = A[s - 1::s], Bv[s - 1::s]
        Bv[s - 1::s] = aR * bL + bR
        A[s - 1::s]  = aR * aL
        s <<= 1
    A[m - 1] = 1.0; Bv[m - 1] = 0.0              # root <- identity
    s = m                                        # ---- down-sweep ----
    while s >= 2:
        h = s >> 1
        ta, tb = A[h - 1::s].copy(), Bv[h - 1::s].copy()   # left aggregate
        A[h - 1::s]  = A[s - 1::s]                         # left <- prefix
        Bv[h - 1::s] = Bv[s - 1::s]
        Bv[s - 1::s] = ta * Bv[s - 1::s] + tb              # right <- prefix o left
        A[s - 1::s]  = ta * A[s - 1::s]
        s >>= 1
    return (a0 * Bv + b0)[:n]                    # exclusive -> inclusive

def scan_parallel(abar, bbar, C, D, x):
    h = blelloch_scan(abar, bbar)
    return np.einsum('tpn,tn->tp', h, C) + D * x

# --- (B) S4D: time-INVARIANT, so the whole map is one kernel ---------------
def s4d_kernel(T, N, dt):
    """S4D-Lin poles A_n = -1/2 + i*pi*n, ZOH-discretized."""
    A = -0.5 + 1j * np.pi * np.arange(N)
    Bc = np.ones(N, dtype=complex)
    Cc = (RNG.normal(size=N) + 1j * RNG.normal(size=N)) / np.sqrt(N)
    Abar = np.exp(dt * A)                        # ZOH state matrix
    Bbar = (Abar - 1.0) / A * Bc                 # ZOH input matrix
    powers = Abar[None, :] ** np.arange(T)[:, None]
    K = 2.0 * np.real(powers @ (Cc * Bbar))      # conj pairs -> real kernel
    return K, Abar, Bbar, Cc

def conv_fft(u, K):
    L = 1 << (2 * len(u) - 1).bit_length()        # zero-pad so it cannot wrap
    return np.fft.irfft(np.fft.rfft(u, L) * np.fft.rfft(K, L), L)[:len(u)]

def conv_naive(u, K):
    T = len(u)
    idx = np.arange(T)[:, None] - np.arange(T)[None, :]
    M = np.where(idx >= 0, K[np.abs(idx)], 0.0)  # lower-triangular Toeplitz
    return M @ u

def lti_recurrence(u, Abar, Bbar, Cc):
    h = np.zeros_like(Abar); y = np.empty(len(u))
    for t, ut in enumerate(u):
        h = Abar * h + Bbar * ut
        y[t] = 2.0 * np.real(Cc @ h)
    return y

# --- (C) SSD: linear recurrence vs masked matmul ---------------------------
def make_ssd(T, P, N, rng):
    log_a = -np.exp(rng.normal(-1.0, 0.4, size=T))          # log a_t < 0
    B = rng.normal(size=(T, N)) / np.sqrt(N)
    C = rng.normal(size=(T, N)) / np.sqrt(N)
    X = rng.normal(size=(T, P))
    return log_a, B, C, X

def ssd_linear(log_a, B, C, X):
    T, N = B.shape; P = X.shape[1]
    a = np.exp(log_a); h = np.zeros((N, P)); Y = np.empty((T, P))
    for t in range(T):
        h = a[t] * h + np.outer(B[t], X[t])      # rank-1 state write
        Y[t] = C[t] @ h
    return Y

def semiseparable_mask(log_a):
    g = np.cumsum(log_a)
    E = np.tril(g[:, None] - g[None, :])         # mask first...
    return np.tril(np.exp(E))                    # ...then exponentiate

def ssd_quadratic(log_a, B, C, X):
    """Y = (L o C B^T) X. Mask the exponent BEFORE exponentiating: above the
    diagonal it is large and positive, exp() overflows to inf, and inf*0 = nan."""
    return (semiseparable_mask(log_a) * (C @ B.T)) @ X

def timed(fn, *args):
    t0 = time.perf_counter(); out = fn(*args)
    return out, time.perf_counter() - t0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    T, P, N = 4096, 64, 16
    print(f"selective SSM: T={T} P={P} N={N}  (state = P*N = {P*N} scalars/layer)")
    abar, bbar, Cs, Ds, xs = make_selective(T, P, N, RNG)
    y_seq, t_seq = timed(scan_sequential, abar, bbar, Cs, Ds, xs)
    y_par, t_par = timed(scan_parallel,   abar, bbar, Cs, Ds, xs)
    r = np.max(np.abs(y_seq - y_par)) / np.max(np.abs(y_seq))
    print(f"  sequential recurrence   {t_seq*1e3:8.1f} ms   depth O(T)")
    print(f"  Blelloch parallel scan  {t_par*1e3:8.1f} ms   depth O(log T) "
          f"= {int(np.ceil(np.log2(T)))} levels")
    print(f"  max rel. difference     {r:.3e}")
    assert r < 1e-6, r

    Tc, Nc, dt = 4096, 64, 0.01
    K, Abar, Bbar, Cc = s4d_kernel(Tc, Nc, dt)
    u = RNG.normal(size=Tc)
    y_fft, t_fft = timed(conv_fft, u, K)
    y_nai, t_nai = timed(conv_naive, u, K)
    y_rec, t_rec = timed(lti_recurrence, u, Abar, Bbar, Cc)
    r_fft = np.max(np.abs(y_fft - y_nai)) / np.max(np.abs(y_nai))
    r_rec = np.max(np.abs(y_rec - y_nai)) / np.max(np.abs(y_nai))
    print(f"\nS4D convolution: T={Tc} N={Nc} dt={dt}")
    print(f"  FFT convolution         {t_fft*1e3:8.1f} ms   O(T log T)")
    print(f"  naive Toeplitz matmul   {t_nai*1e3:8.1f} ms   O(T^2)")
    print(f"  step-by-step recurrence {t_rec*1e3:8.1f} ms   O(T N)")
    print(f"  rel. err FFT vs naive       {r_fft:.3e}")
    print(f"  rel. err recurrence vs conv {r_rec:.3e}")
    assert r_fft < 1e-6 and r_rec < 1e-6, (r_fft, r_rec)

    Ts, Ps, Ns = 2048, 64, 64
    log_a, Bq, Cq, Xq = make_ssd(Ts, Ps, Ns, RNG)
    Y_lin,  t_lin  = timed(ssd_linear,    log_a, Bq, Cq, Xq)
    Y_quad, t_quad = timed(ssd_quadratic, log_a, Bq, Cq, Xq)
    r_ssd = np.max(np.abs(Y_lin - Y_quad)) / np.max(np.abs(Y_lin))
    print(f"\nSSD duality: T={Ts} P={Ps} N={Ns}")
    print(f"  linear recurrent form   {t_lin*1e3:8.1f} ms   O(T N P) time, O(N P) state")
    print(f"  quadratic masked matmul {t_quad*1e3:8.1f} ms   O(T^2 N) time, O(T^2) memory")
    print(f"  MAX REL DIFFERENCE      {r_ssd:.3e}   <-- the duality")
    assert r_ssd < 1e-5, r_ssd

    # Every strictly-lower submatrix of L has rank one: L[t,s] = e^{g_t} e^{-g_s}.
    Lmask = semiseparable_mask(log_a)
    sv = np.linalg.svd(Lmask[1024:1044, 1000:1020], compute_uv=False)
    print(f"  off-diagonal 20x20 block singular values: "
          f"s1={sv[0]:.3e}  s2/s1={sv[1]/sv[0]:.2e}  (rank 1)")
    assert sv[1] / sv[0] < 1e-12

    if torch is None:
        print("\n[skipped: torch not installed]")
    else:
        with torch.no_grad():
            ut, Kt = torch.from_numpy(u), torch.from_numpy(K)
            Lp = 1 << (2 * Tc - 1).bit_length()
            yt = torch.fft.irfft(torch.fft.rfft(ut, Lp) * torch.fft.rfft(Kt, Lp),
                                 Lp)[:Tc].numpy()
            Mt = torch.from_numpy(Lmask * (Cq @ Bq.T)) @ torch.from_numpy(Xq)
        print(f"\n[torch] FFT conv rel. err   "
              f"{np.max(np.abs(yt - y_nai))/np.max(np.abs(y_nai)):.3e}")
        print(f"[torch] SSD matmul rel. err "
              f"{np.max(np.abs(Mt.numpy() - Y_lin))/np.max(np.abs(Y_lin)):.3e}")
    print("\nall assertions passed")

The run completes in under 4 s. The two scan forms agree to a relative $1.845\times10^{-16}$ — machine precision, since they perform the same additions in a different order. FFT convolution matches the naive Toeplitz product to $4.320\times10^{-16}$ and the recurrence matches to $8.780\times10^{-15}$, at about $2$ ms against $800$ ms at $T=4096$. The duality assertion holds at $4.211\times10^{-14}$ ($T=2048$, $N=P=64$), and the $20\times20$ off-diagonal block of $L$ has $\sigma_2/\sigma_1 = 3.57\times10^{-17}$. One timing cuts against the story: the Blelloch scan takes roughly $700$ ms against $15$–$19$ ms for the sequential loop. NumPy on one core gives it no parallelism while charging strided, non-contiguous access: the $\log T$ depth is a latency claim that pays only on hardware with $T/2$ lanes, hence a CUDA kernel. The residuals are deterministic; the wall-clock figures are machine-dependent. Verify

Under Encryption

An SSM is a sequential recurrence, and sequential is what multiplicative depth punishes. Each step $h_t = \bar a_t h_{t-1} + \bar b_t$ is one ciphertext–ciphertext multiplication when $\bar a_t$ is itself encrypted, so a naive encrypted scan over $n$ tokens consumes depth $\Theta(n)$ — hundreds of bootstraps at any useful sequence length. The parallel-scan form is the interesting one: Blelloch's $O(\log n)$ parallel depth is also $O(\log n)$ multiplicative depth, because each level of the tree applies $\oplus$ once and $\oplus$ costs one multiplication. That turns 4096 levels into 24. Better still, $\oplus$ needs no softmax, no exponential of a ciphertext, no comparison — only multiply and add, which is exactly the polynomial fragment CKKS evaluates cheaply. The SSD form is even friendlier: it is a masked matrix multiply, and matmul is the one thing FHE does well; the mask $L$ can be computed from public or client-supplied $\Delta$ and folded in as a plaintext multiplication, which costs no depth at all. On that reasoning an SSM is a better fit for homomorphic evaluation than attention. Whether it has been done at scale is close to open: Brito's public-decay homomorphic state space models (arXiv 2605.16647, May 2026) report an encrypted SSM classifier running at depth 8 with ring dimension 32768, against depth 10 and ring 65536 for polynomial attention on the same task, roughly $5\times$ faster — but that is a fastText-feature sentiment classifier, not a language model. Verify Chapter 39 takes up the approximation problem in detail, and Chapter 42 still lists encrypted long-sequence SSM inference among the open problems rather than the solved ones.

Key Takeaways
  • A linear time-invariant recurrence is a convolution: ZOH discretization gives $\bar A = e^{\Delta A}$, $\bar B = A^{-1}(e^{\Delta A}-I)B$, and $K_\ell = C\bar A^\ell \bar B$, so training runs an FFT in $O(T\log T)$ and inference runs the recurrence in $O(N)$ per token. Certain
  • HiPPO is not a heuristic: the coefficients of the optimal Legendre projection of the input history satisfy exactly a linear ODE, and its matrix is normal-plus-rank-one, which is what makes the S4 kernel computable in $\tilde O(N+T)$ via Woodbury and a Cauchy kernel. Certain
  • Selectivity means $\Delta_t, B_t, C_t$ depend on $x_t$; this is precisely what LTI forbids and precisely what content-based recall requires. It costs the FFT and buys gating, leaving an associative scan — $2T-2$ work, $2\lceil \log_2 T\rceil$ depth — as the only parallel training algorithm. Certain
  • SSD: with $\bar A_t = a_tI$, the recurrence equals $Y = (L\odot CB^\top)X$ with $L$ 1-semiseparable — masked attention with softmax deleted and the binary mask replaced by a decay mask. The artifact asserts this to $4.2\times10^{-14}$. Certain
  • Pure SSMs do not replace transformers: they win on perplexity-per-FLOP and lose on in-context recall, and the near-universal adoption of hybrids is the field's own verdict. Mamba-3 (2026) narrows the gap with complex transitions and half the state; treat any claim about the frontier as dated. Contested
